claims.text: Moderate cooling rates permit dynamic short-range order to form within the high-temperature BCC matrix.
Short-range-order domains locally modulate the elemental distribution.
Short-range-order domains lower the nucleation barrier for secondary phases.
Short-range order formed during cooling directs phase transformations during subsequent thermal exposure.
Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be prepared as a high-temperature single-phase BCC solid solution.
Water quenching from the high-temperature state suppresses atomic mobility and short-range-order formation.
Controlled furnace cooling allows sufficient diffusion for short-range-order development.
The proposed pathway operates where atomic mobility during cooling is moderate.
Locally enriched or depleted short-range-order regions act as nucleation sites for secondary phases.
Possible secondary phases include metastable FCC phases or ordered intermetallic phases.
Bulk diffusion in the high-entropy alloy is sluggish but sufficient at moderate cooling rates to form short-range order.
Rapid quenching largely retains the BCC structure by suppressing short-range-order development.
Extremely slow cooling or prolonged annealing eventually drives the system toward equilibrium configurations and complete phase separation.
After identical annealing, slowly cooled samples will have a higher secondary-phase fraction than water-quenched samples.
After identical annealing, secondary phases will appear earlier in slowly cooled samples than in water-quenched samples.
The extent of phase transformation correlates with the amount of short-range order developed during cooling.
The rapidly quenched baseline largely retains the high-temperature BCC structure and contains minimal short-range order.
The mechanism should not govern phase evolution under ultra-rapid cooling because diffusion is nearly frozen.
The mechanism should cease to govern phase evolution after extremely long annealing because equilibrium phase separation overprints short-range order.

Failure of slowly cooled samples to show a statistically significant increase in both secondary-phase fraction and short-range-order-related features relative to the quenched control would falsify the hypothesis.
